nodes.label: Provenance Tracking Rationale
nodes.rationale: Every computed value is tagged with provenance (api/config/estimate) so UI can show data quality badges and users know whether rates came from live APIs or static fallback files. This is critical for trust in a cost calculator: a value from the Core fuel API feed is more reliable than a config fallback, and the system communicates this distinction explicitly.

nodes.label: Graceful Degradation / Fallback Chain Rationale
nodes.rationale: The system uses a layered fallback strategy: live API first (Google Maps, ORS, Core fuel), then config-based estimates (haversine x road_factor, fallback-rates.json diesel prices). This ensures the app always returns a cost estimate even when external APIs are unavailable, while communicating data quality through the provenance system.

nodes.label: Zero-Based Costing Methodology
nodes.rationale: Freight costs are decomposed into 10 independent cost heads (fuel, driver, vehicle, toll, maintenance, loading, idle, overhead, risk, empty_return), each calculated from first principles rather than quoting market rates. This allows fleet operators to audit each component and identify where actual costs deviate from benchmarks.
